title: omaddons vision, architecture and milestone roadmap (M1–M5)
description:
# omaddons — vision, architecture, milestone roadmap

Living document. External facts verified 2026-10-14 unless marked UNVERIFIED.

## 1. Thesis

`omaddons` is a single Rust binary that is the sole authority over every World of Warcraft client on a Linux machine: Battle.net under Wine/Proton/umu (Omarchy's default), Steam/Lutris/Heroic/Bottles prefixes, and custom private-server clients such as 3.3.5a (AzerothCore). It discovers every client, manages addons per client ("target") transactionally, and exposes everything through a stable, machine-readable CLI contract. Coding agents drive the CLI directly. Humans use a thin Omarchy bar widget that renders CLI output and holds no logic of its own. Every mutation is journaled and snapshotted, so any change, human- or agent-initiated, is reversible with `omaddons undo`.

Framing: **the CLI is the product, the widget is a view, the agent skill is the manual.**

## 2. Goals and non-goals

Goals:
- **G1 Multi-target.** All installed flavors managed simultaneously: retail, progression Classic, Classic Era, Anniversary, Forever, PTR/XPTR/beta, plus custom clients (3.3.5a) as first-class targets.
- **G2 Zero-config, keyless by default.** Discovery needs no setup; the most-used addons install and update without any account. CurseForge and Wago are optional bring-your-own-credential sources; nothing depends on them.
- **G3 Reliability.** No operation can leave an addon half-installed; crashes recover on next run; concurrent invocations (widget + terminal + agent) are safe; upstream schema drift yields typed errors, never crashes or unparseable output.
- **G4 Agent-first ergonomics.** Versioned JSON envelope, stable error codes with hints and candidates, `--dry-run` parity, `next` command suggestions, idempotency, never prompts without a TTY, token-frugal output, shipped skill/guide, machine-readable output schemas.
- **G5 Verifiable privacy.** Hard host allowlist (redirects included), local request log, `--offline`, no telemetry, no CurseForge data persisted.
- **G6 Correct by the game's rules.** Compatibility decided by applying the client's TOC loading rules to the actual archive contents, not by upstream metadata alone.
- **G7 Diagnostics.** `doctor` findings each carry an executable fix; Lua errors captured by BugGrabber are attributed to addons.
- **G8 Omarchy-native widget** following the house plugin pattern, always version-locked to the binary.

Non-goals:
- No standalone GUI or TUI; no daemon; no MCP server in v1 (the command layer returns typed results so an MCP adapter is a thin later addition).
- No WeakAuras/Wago string management, ElvUI profile management, or SavedVariables editing.
- No Windows/macOS support (code may stay portable; untested and unsupported).
- No CurseForge proxy, no bundled API keys.
- No addon authoring or packaging.

## 3. Reference project audit

Reference: https://github.com/BabaStardust/Omarchy-WoW-Addons-Plugin at commit 5c35a8f (v1.1.1, MIT). Omarchy bar widget (`Panel.qml`, ~1000 lines QML) + `bin/wowaddons` (750-line stdlib Python) calling CurseForge API v1 with a user-supplied key. Audit found no telemetry or malicious behavior; network limited to api.curseforge.com, the CurseForge CDN, and xdg-open of user-clicked links.

Ideas worth keeping: argv-only process invocation (no shell), API key passed via stdin and stored mode 0600 with atomic writes, zip path-traversal checks, checksum verification, honoring `allowModDistribution=false` with a manual-download import flow, `Text.PlainText` rendering of all API strings in QML.

Defects this design must fix (line refs into `bin/wowaddons` / `Panel.qml` at 5c35a8f):

| # | Reference behavior | Consequence | omaddons mechanism |
|---|---|---|---|
| R1 | One AddOns dir resolved by glob + folder-name guess; auto-picks only `*forever*`/`*classic_beta*` folders (`resolve()`, l.132-149; comment promises a classic fallback that is not implemented) | Retail-only install resolves to `no-flavor`; custom layouts (`drive_c/WoW`) never detected | Discovery from `.build.info` + `.flavor.info` + PE version; many named targets |
| R2 | `install_zip` rmtree's previous folders, then per folder rmtree + `os.replace` (l.339-349); state recorded afterwards | Failure mid-loop leaves an addon partially replaced or deleted with stale records | Stage → rename-swap → journal → recovery; snapshot-based undo |
| R3 | `main` catches only `Failure`/`ValueError` (l.741-746) | KeyError on API drift or OSError in rmtree prints a traceback and no JSON; panel shows "no response". JSONDecodeError surfaces as "Invalid argument" | Typed error model; panic hook still emits the JSON envelope |
| R4 | Read-modify-write of `installed.json` without a lock; fixed `.tmp` name (`write_json`, l.99-105) | Concurrent widget + CLI/agent can lose updates or clobber the temp file | flock for mutations; unique temp + rename for every write |
| R5 | Zip top-level directories used verbatim (l.331) | `Foo-main/` and `Foo-main/Foo/` layouts install broken | Addon-root detection by TOC; name normalization |
| R6 | File choice = max fileId per gameVersionTypeId; default releaseType 3 = alpha (l.47, l.237-247) | Alpha builds by default; no check the client will load the file | Resolution + TOC verification; stable channel default |
| R7 | CurseForge-only, key mandatory; caches CurseForge search results (l.436-495) | Useless without a CF console key; CF terms forbid caching API data and say non-developer console accounts may be deleted | Keyless-first; CF opt-in; no CF data cached |
| R8 | Each panel open spawns `list` + `config` + `updates` + featured `search` (two network round trips); ~38 ms Python startup per process (measured with hyperfine) | Latency and network chatter on every open | One local `status --json` read (ms, no network); background checks; file-change doorbell |
| R9 | Unmanaged addons only listed; `Blizzard_*` folders in custom clients appear as unmanaged | No adoption; protected folders exposed to mutation | Adoption by TOC IDs + content hashes; `Blizzard_*` protected at the type level |
| R10 | Background update check can `mkdir` the AddOns folder (l.157-160) despite README "nothing written without a click" | Surprising writes | Read paths never write to game directories |
| R11 | URLs from API passed to `xdg-open` unchecked (`Panel.qml` l.109) | Arbitrary scheme handlers reachable | Only `https` URLs to allowlisted web hosts are opened |
| R12 | Agent support is an AGENTS.md key-setup walkthrough | No machine contract | Full agent contract (§5.8–5.9) |

Language note: most improvements are design, not language. Rust is chosen for a self-contained binary with no interpreter dependency, ~1–2 ms startup for the high-frequency widget/agent calls, type-level enforcement of safety invariants (folder names that cannot escape AddOns or name protected folders; exhaustive error mapping), and simple bounded concurrency.

## 4. Verified external facts

### 4.1 Battle.net installs

- Omarchy installs Battle.net via umu-launcher + GE-Proton into `WINEPREFIX=~/Games/battlenet` (`omarchy-install-gaming-battlenet`), launched by `omarchy-launch-battlenet`. WoW root: `~/Games/battlenet/drive_c/Program Files (x86)/World of Warcraft/`.
- `<root>/.build.info` is BPSV: one header row of pipe-separated `Name!TYPE:size` columns, then one row per installed product. Columns changed over the years (KeyService, KeyRing, Product added later): **parse by header name, never by position**. Relevant columns: `Product`, `Version` (e.g. `12.1.5.70391`), `Active` (`1`), `Branch` (`us`/`eu`), `Tags` (contains spaces, `?`, `:`). Example header: `Branch!STRING:0|Active!DEC:1|Build Key!HEX:16|CDN Key!HEX:16|Install Key!HEX:16|IM Size!DEC:4|CDN Path!STRING:0|CDN Hosts!STRING:0|CDN Servers!STRING:0|Tags!STRING:0|Armadillo!STRING:0|Last Activated!STRING:0|Version!STRING:0|KeyRing!HEX:16|Product!STRING:0`. Format reference: https://wowdev.wiki/TACT
- Each flavor folder `<root>/_<x>_/` contains `.flavor.info` (BPSV header `Product Flavor!STRING:0`, value = product code): authoritative folder → product mapping.
- Products (Blizzard productconfig `shared_container_default_subfolder`, mirrored at https://github.com/Arctium/bnet-tact-channel-configs; prior art: instawow `wow_installations.py`, WowUp `warcraft-platform.linux.ts`):

| Product | Folder | Exe | Version (Oct 2026) |
|---|---|---|---|
| wow | `_retail_` | WoW.exe | 12.1.5.70391 |
| wowt | `_ptr_` | WoWT.exe | 12.1.0 |
| wowxptr | `_xptr_` | WoWT.exe | 12.1.5 |
| wow_beta | `_beta_` | WoWB.exe | 12.0.1 |
| wow_classic | `_classic_` | WoWClassic.exe | 5.5.4 (Mists) |
| wow_classic_ptr | `_classic_ptr_` | WoWClassicT.exe | 5.5.4 |
| wow_classic_beta | `_classic_beta_` | WowB.exe | 1.60.1.70374 (Forever beta) |
| wow_classic_era | `_classic_era_` | WoWClassic.exe | 1.15.9 |
| wow_classic_era_ptr | `_classic_era_ptr_` | WowClassicT.exe | 2.5.6 (Anniversary PTR) |
| wow_anniversary | `_anniversary_` | WoWClassic.exe | 2.5.6 (TBC) |
| wow_classic_titan | `_classic_titan_` | WoWClassic.exe | 3.80.2 (China) |
| wowf | `_forever_` | Wow.exe | 1.60.1.70245 |

- **Product code does not determine game family** (`wow_classic_era_ptr` runs TBC 2.5.x; `wow_classic_beta` runs Forever 1.60.x). Family is derived from version; product is a label and fallback. Exe names vary in case: match case-insensitively. Folder names are not derivable by pattern (`wowf` → `_forever_`).
- Version → family table (data, overridable in config): major 1 & minor < 50 → `vanilla` (era); major 1 & minor ≥ 50 → `forever`; 2.5 → `tbc`; 3.4 → `wrath`; 3.80 → `titan`; 4.4 → `cata`; 5.5 → `mists`; major ≥ 6 → `mainline`/standard (retail). 3.3.x on a custom client → `wrath-legacy`.
- Interface number = major×10000 + minor×100 + patch: 12.1.5 → 120105; 1.60.1 → 16001; 3.80.2 → 38002; 3.3.5 → 30300.
- Current interfaces (https://warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/TOC_format): Retail 120105 · Mists Classic 50504 · Classic Era 11509 · Anniversary/TBC 20506 · Titan 38002 · Cata 40402 · Forever 16001 (beta/test).
- WoW: Forever ("Classic+", announced BlizzCon 2026): launch 2026-11-04; level cap 60, new content. Product `wowf` / folder `_forever_` first appeared in productconfig 2026-10-13 (uninstall strings "World of Warcraft Forever", "WoW: Forever - Stress Test"). Beta currently installs to `_classic_beta_`. Final launch layout is UNVERIFIED; detection must be data-driven so any new `_x_` folder works without code changes.

### 4.2 Custom clients (3.3.5a)

- Layout: `<root>/Wow.exe`, `<root>/Interface/AddOns/`, `<root>/WTF/`, `<root>/Data/<locale>/realmlist.wtf` containing `set realmlist <host>` (location valid 3.0.2–5.0.4, https://warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Realmlist.wtf). No `.build.info`, no flavor folder.
- Version: Wow.exe PE `VS_FIXEDFILEINFO` numeric fields (3.3.5.12340 = 3.3.5a). Read numeric fields, not the version string (string form UNVERIFIED).
- Private-server client packs may ship extracted `Blizzard_*` addons inside `Interface/AddOns`; these must never be modified.
- 3.3.5a reads only `Folder/Folder.toc` (multi-TOC arrived in 9.1.0/1.13.7/2.5.1; comma Interface lists in 10.2.7). Treat as single-TOC, single-Interface. `Dependencies`, `OptionalDeps`, `LoadOnDemand`, `LoadWith`, `LoadManagers` predate it.
- No `release.json` flavor and no WoWInterface compatibility tag covers 3.3.5: sources are GitHub releases/repos, git, URLs, local zips.

### 4.3 TOC format and load rules (https://warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/TOC_format)

- TOC basename must equal the folder name. The client reads only the first 1024 characters of each line.
- Game-specific suffixes: `_Standard` (retail, since 12.1.5), `_Forever` / `_Camelot` (internal game type `camelot`), `_Mists`, `_Cata`, `_Wrath`, `_TBC` (also Anniversary), `_Vanilla`, `_Plunderstorm` / `_WoWLabs`, `_WoWHack`. Family suffixes: `_Mainline` (standard, forever, plunderstorm, wowhack), `_Classic` (vanilla…mists). Legacy `_BCC`, `_WOTLKC` are dropped by current clients but appear in the wild. Wago data and managers accept `-` or `_` separators.
- Precedence: game-specific suffix > family suffix > plain `Name.toc`; exactly one TOC is loaded. **A Forever client loads a retail-only `_Mainline.toc`** (family Mainline): verification must also check `## Interface`.
- Comma lists `## Interface: 120105, 50504, 11509` supported since 10.2.7.
- Directives: `Dependencies` (aliases `RequiredDeps` and any directive starting with `Dep`), `OptionalDeps`, `LoadOnDemand`, `LoadWith`, `LoadManagers`, `AllowLoadGameType` / `ExcludeLoadGameType`, inline file conditionals (`retail.lua [AllowLoadGameType standard]`), directive conditionals (12.0.7+), path variables `[Family]`, `[Game]`, `[TextLocale]`. `## Interface-Vanilla:`-style lines are BigWigs-packager build-time only (not read by the client).
- Source-identifying fields: `X-Curse-Project-ID`, `X-WoWI-ID`, `X-Wago-ID`, `X-Tukui-ProjectID`, `X-Tukui-ProjectFolders`, `X-Website`, `X-AddonProvider`, `X-Part-Of`; plus `## Version`, `## Title`, `## Author`, `## Notes`. The packager substitutes `@project-version@` tokens; it adds no `X-*` lines.

### 4.4 WTF, SavedVariables, BugGrabber, running clients

- Account SavedVariables: `WTF/Account/<ACCT>/SavedVariables/<Addon>.lua`; character: `WTF/Account/<ACCT>/<Realm>/<Char>/SavedVariables/<Addon>.lua`; Blizzard's own: `WTF/Account/<ACCT>/SavedVariables.lua`. `<ACCT>` is e.g. `123456#1` (Battle.net) or a legacy account name. Account, realm and character names are personal data: never in default output.
- Per-character `AddOns.txt` (`Name: enabled|disabled`); modern format UNVERIFIED.
- `WTF/Config.wtf` `SET lastAddonVersion "<interface>"` (fallback interface source). CVar `checkAddonVersion` (default 1) gates loading out-of-date addons; the "Load out of date AddOns" checkbox resets each patch (storage location UNVERIFIED).
- SavedVariables load just before `ADDON_LOADED` and are written on logout, disconnect, quit and `/reload`; external edits made while the client runs are overwritten.
- BugGrabber stores errors in account SavedVariables `!BugGrabber.lua`, global `BugGrabberDB`:
  - Modern (v12.x): `{session=N, lastSanitation=3, stopnag=?, errors={...}}`, max 500 errors, oldest dropped; each error `{message=string, stack=string?, locals=string?, session=int, time=unix_epoch_int, counter=int}` (stack/locals absent for simple errors). Mirror: https://github.com/hippuli/BugGrabber
  - Legacy r152 (`## Interface: 30300`, common in 3.3.5 packs, e.g. https://github.com/Evolvee/EvolvePWPUI-335a): errors `{message=string | table of ≤980-char chunks, session, time="%Y/%m/%d %H:%M:%S" string, type, counter}`; stack and locals embedded in `message` after `"\nLocals:|r\n"`; DB also has `limit=50`, `save`, `throttle`.
  - Stack frames reference `Interface\AddOns\<Folder>\…` (or `/`) → folder attribution.
- Updating while running: modern clients pick up new files, new addons and TOC changes on `/reload` (since 9.0.1 retail / 1.14.0 era); deleting or renaming an already-loaded TOC needs a client restart. 3.3.5a likely needs a full restart for new addons or TOC changes (UNVERIFIED).

### 4.5 Addon sources

**GitHub releases + BigWigs packager `release.json`** (https://github.com/BigWigsMods/packager, `upload_github()` in `release.sh`):
- Asset `release.json`: `{"releases":[{"name","version","filename","nolib":false,"metadata":[{"flavor":"mainline","interface":120100}]}]}`; an additional entry with `nolib:true` may exist. Only `filename`, `nolib`, `metadata` are reliable (Questie omits `name`/`version` and adds extra keys).
- Flavor names: `mainline, classic, bcc, wrath, cata, mists, titan, forever` (packager maps tbc→bcc, vanilla→classic, wotlkc→wrath, camelot→forever).
- Publishing `release.json` (Oct 2026): WeakAuras2, DBM, BigWigs, LittleWigs, Plater, Bartender4, Questie, OmniCC, Dominos, Masque, RaiderIO, MythicDungeonTools, AllTheThings. WeakAuras' current `release.json` has **no `mainline` entry** (metadata unreliable → verify TOCs). Details! has no usable GitHub releases (latest 2021).
- REST rate limit: 60 req/h/IP unauthenticated, 5000/h authenticated; conditional-request 304s are free only when authenticated (https://docs.github.com/en/rest/using-the-rest-api/best-practices-for-using-the-rest-api). Non-REST fallback: `https://github.com/<o>/<r>/releases/latest` redirects to the latest non-prerelease tag; assets at `https://github.com/<o>/<r>/releases/download/<tag>/<file>`.

**WoWInterface / MMOUI v3 (keyless, live):**
- `GET https://api.mmoui.com/v3/game/WOW/filelist.json` (~5.6 MB, ~8.2k entries, `Cache-Control: max-age=3600`): `UID, UICATID, UIVersion, UIDate (ms), UIName, UIAuthorName, UIFileInfoURL, UIDownloadTotal, UIDownloadMonthly, UIFavoriteTotal, UICompatibility[{version,name}]|null, UIDir[], UIIMG_Thumbs, UIIMGs, UISiblings`.
- `GET https://api.mmoui.com/v3/game/WOW/filedetails/<id>[,<id>…].json` (comma batch): adds `UIMD5, UIFileName, UIDownload` (`https://cdn.wowinterface.com/downloads/getfile.php?id=…&d=…&minion`), `UIPending, UIDescription, UIChangeLog`.
- Flavor support weak (only `UICompatibility`, single main file): effectively retail-centric.

**Tukui (keyless):** `GET https://api.tukui.org/v1/addons` (ElvUI id -2, Tukui id -1), `GET https://api.tukui.org/v1/addon/<slug>`: `id, slug, name, author, version, url` (download), `patch[]` (e.g. `["12.1.0","5.5.4","1.15.9","2.5.6"]` = supported client versions), `directories[], last_update, changelog_url, git_url, web_url`.

**CurseForge (optional, bring-your-own key):**
- Base `https://api.curseforge.com`, header `x-api-key`; no key → 403. Docs: https://docs.curseforge.com/rest-api/
- Keys: self-serve via console.curseforge.com (create org → key) observed working in 2025, but docs state "Any registered account which is not a game developer and did not request a key, will be deleted"; the official third-party route is an application form reviewed by Overwolf (https://support.curseforge.com/support/solutions/articles/9000208346). Third-party API terms: a key "is non-transferable and may not be shared with any third party"; prohibited: "accessing the API through a proxy server or VPN" and "save or cache any data obtained through the API". End users' personal keys inside a distributed tool are not addressed → treat as fragile; never required.
- CDN: CurseForge announced (2026-06-10) that `edge.forgecdn.net` downloads require `x-api-key` (or `?api-key=`) from 2026-07-16 (keyless download still worked 2026-10-14: 302 → `mediafilez.forgecdn.net` → 206). Always send the key.
- Endpoints (WoW gameId 1): `GET /v1/mods/search?gameId=1&gameVersionTypeId&searchFilter&slug&classId=1&categoryId&sortField&sortOrder&index&pageSize` (pageSize ≤ 50; index+pageSize ≤ 10000); `POST /v1/mods {modIds, filterPcOnly}`; `GET /v1/mods/{id}/files[/{fileId}]`; `POST /v1/mods/files {fileIds}`; `GET /v1/mods/{id}/files/{fileId}/download-url`; `GET /v1/mods/{id}/files/{fileId}/changelog`; `POST /v1/fingerprints[/{gameId}] {"fingerprints":[u32]}` → `isCacheBuilt, exactMatches[{id,file,latestFiles}], exactFingerprints, partialMatches, partialMatchFingerprints, installedFingerprints, unmatchedFingerprints` (match on `file.modules[].fingerprint`); `POST /v1/fingerprints/fuzzy[/{gameId}]`.
- `allowModDistribution: bool|null`; `false` ⇒ `downloadUrl` null ⇒ manual browser download + `import`.
- gameVersionTypeId: Retail 517 · Classic Era 67408 · TBC/Anniversary 73246 · Wrath 73713 · Cata 77522 · Mists 79434 · Titan 81212 · Forever 88568.
- Folder fingerprint (WowUp `curse-folder-scanner.ts` + `native/curse.cc`): file set = `<Dir>/<Dir>[-_](mainline|bcc|tbc|classic|vanilla|wrath|wotlkc|cata|mists|forever|camelot)?.toc` + `<Dir>/Bindings.xml` + recursively every `.lua`/`.xml` referenced by TOC lines (after stripping `#` comments) and by `<Include|Script file="…">` in XML (after stripping `<!-- -->`); reject `..`; resolve paths case-insensitively; skip missing; count each file once. Per file: MurmurHash2 (m = 1540483477, seed 1) over the bytes with 0x09/0x0A/0x0D/0x20 removed (length = stripped length). Per folder: sort per-file u32 ascending, concatenate as decimal strings without separator, hash that ASCII string the same way.
- Rate limits undocumented (quota at Overwolf's discretion).

**Wago Addons (optional, paid token):**
- Public keyless `GET https://addons.wago.io/api/data/game`: per-flavor patches, `toc_suffixes`, `live_patches` (usable as a flavor/interface cross-check).
- Manager API (undocumented) `https://addons.wago.io/api/external`, `Authorization: Bearer <token>`, downloads take `?token=`; 401 without. `GET /addons/_search?query&game_version&stability`, `GET /addons/popular`, `GET /addons/{id}`, `POST /addons/_recents {game_version, addons:[ids]}`, `POST /addons/_match {game_version, addons:[{name, hash, cf?, wowi?, wago?}]}` where `hash` = MD5 of the sorted per-file MD5 hex strings over the TOC-derived file set. `game_version` ∈ retail|classic|bc|wotlk|cata|mop|forever; `stability` ∈ stable|beta|alpha. Tokens come from a Patreon tier ("Wago Access Key"); WowUp uses an ad-page token.

**Prior art:** instawow (Python; CF via user key `access_tokens.cfcore`; sources CF, WoWI, Tukui, Wago, GitHub), WowUp (Electron; CF only in the Overwolf build with an embedded key), Ajour (Rust, archived; dropped CF 2021–22; check license before reusing code), strongbox and CurseBreaker (dropped CF).

### 4.6 Omarchy plugin system

- A plugin is a folder with `manifest.json` at its root under `~/.config/omarchy/plugins/<id>/`, loaded into the long-lived `omarchy-shell` (Quickshell/QML), unsandboxed. Saving any file under the plugins directory hot-reloads plugin code. Docs: `~/.local/share/omarchy/shell/README.md`; schema enforced by `shell/services/PluginRegistry.qml` and mirrored by `omarchy-plugin-validate`.
- Validation: `schemaVersion` exactly 1; required `id, name, version, kinds, entryPoints`; id `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]*$`, no `..`, not `omarchy.*`; entry points relative, existing, no `..`; kinds `bar|bar-widget|menu|overlay|panel|service` each require their entry point key (`bar-widget` → `entryPoints.barWidget`); `barWidget.defaultSection` ∈ left|center|right; **no symlinks anywhere in the plugin folder**. This repository contains `AGENTS.md → CLAUDE.md`, so the repository root can never be the plugin.
- Non-git install is supported: write the folder, `omarchy-shell shell rescanPlugins`, `omarchy plugin enable <id> [--section …]`. `omarchy plugin update` applies only to git checkouts (shows a diff, asks, fast-forwards, re-validates).
- House plugin pattern (a44.herd, a44.beads, a44.docker): `manifest.json` + `Panel.qml` (view) + `Service.qml` (state + `Process` calls) + `Model.js` (pure helpers). The CLI is the authority; an event source is a "doorbell" that triggers a re-fetch of the authority, never a source of state. Settings via manifest `barWidget.defaults` + `barWidget.schema` (types `string|integer|enum|command|path`). Quickshell `FileView { watchChanges: true }` is available (used in shell `Commons/Style.qml`). Plugin id for this project: `a44.omaddons`.

### 4.7 Development machine (real-world oracle)

- Retail: `~/Games/battlenet/drive_c/Program Files (x86)/World of Warcraft/`; `.build.info` product `wow`, version `12.1.0.69933` (interface 120100; live is 12.1.5); only `_retail_`; AddOns empty.
- Custom: `~/Games/wow-335/drive_c/WoW/` (Wow.exe 3.3.5a; `Interface/AddOns` holds 23 `Blizzard_*` folders and nothing else; `Data/enUS/realmlist.wtf` = `set realmlist 127.0.0.1`, a local AzerothCore server).
- Toolchain present: cargo/rustc 1.95 (nightly default), cargo-deny, cargo-audit, cargo-llvm-cov, cargo-fuzz, hyperfine, ubs.

## 5. Architecture

```
          ┌──────────── humans ────────────┐        ┌──── agents ────┐
          │ Omarchy widget (QML, embedded) │        │ skill / guide  │
          └──────┬──────────────▲──────────┘        └───────┬────────┘
     runs `omaddons … --json`   │ FileView doorbell         │ runs `omaddons … --json`
                 ▼              │ on status.json            ▼
┌─────────────────────────── omaddons (single Rust binary) ───────────────────────────┐
│ cli (clap) → app (commands return typed outcomes) → output (human | JSON envelope)  │
│ discover   installs → targets (.build.info, .flavor.info, PE version, realmlist)     │
│ toc        parser + client load-rule engine          doctor   findings + fixes      │
│ sources    github · wowi · tukui · git · url · local · curseforge* · wago*          │
│ resolve    candidate selection + TOC verification against target                    │
│ install    inspect → stage → swap → journal → snapshot → undo/recover               │
│ state      config.toml · targets/*.json · history.jsonl · status.json · lock        │
│ net        allowlist · net.log · ETag cache · retry/backoff · bounded parallelism   │
│ lua        SavedVariables literal parser (BugGrabber)    omarchy  widget installer  │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                                   * credential required, opt-in
```

### 5.1 Domain model

- **Install**: a WoW root, either a Battle.net root (has `.build.info`) or a custom client root (has `Wow*.exe` + `Interface/`, no `.build.info`).
- **Target**: one AddOns directory plus client identity `{id, install_root, flavor_dir?, product?, family, version, interface, exe_name, label}`. Default ids: `retail`, `classic` (current progression Classic), `era`, `anniversary`, `forever`, `ptr`, `xptr`, `beta`, `classic-ptr`, `classic-beta`, `era-ptr`, `titan`; custom clients named from family (`wotlk`) or by the user. Collisions are qualified by install (`retail@steam`). Unknown flavor folders become targets with family `unknown` and an interface from `.build.info`.
- **Folder**: an `AddOns/<Name>` directory, classified `protected` (`Blizzard_*`), `managed` (owned by exactly one managed addon) or `unmanaged`.
- **Addon (managed)**: one project from one source, owning ≥ 1 folders in one target. Record: `{ref, name, version, release_id, channel, pinned, folders[], folder_hashes{}, installed_at, tx_id}`.
- **Ref**: canonical `source:id` (`gh:WeakAuras/WeakAuras2`, `wowi:5108`, `tukui:elvui`, `cf:61284`, `wago:<id>`, `git:<url>[#<rev>]`, `url:<https-zip>`, `file:<path>`).
- **Release**: a resolved downloadable `{source, version, date, channel, download_url, hashes{}, flavor_evidence, changelog?}`.
- **Transaction**: an atomic change set on one target with journal and snapshot.
- **Finding**: a doctor result `{code, severity, target, addon?, folder?, message, evidence?, fix?, auto_fix}`.

### 5.2 Discovery

1. Candidate prefixes and roots: `~/Games/*/drive_c`, `~/.wine/drive_c`, `~/.local/share/Steam/steamapps/compatdata/*/pfx/drive_c`, Lutris/Heroic prefixes, `~/.local/share/bottles/bottles/*/drive_c`, plus `extra_roots` from config. Under each `drive_c`, bounded-depth search (≤ 4, skipping `windows/` and `users/`) for `World of Warcraft/` directories or any directory containing a `Wow*.exe` (case-insensitive).
2. Battle.net root: parse `.build.info` by header name; enumerate `_*_` folders; product from `.flavor.info` (fallback: `.build.info` product table); version from `.build.info`; family from the version table; interface computed; exe from the folder listing.
3. Custom root: version from PE `VS_FIXEDFILEINFO` (`pelite`), interface computed, AddOns at `<root>/Interface/AddOns`, label from `Data/*/realmlist.wtf` host (`127.0.0.1` → "localhost"); `WTF/Config.wtf lastAddonVersion` as a cross-check.
4. Manual targets: `omaddons targets add <path> [--name N]` (root, flavor folder, or AddOns path accepted and normalized); `targets rm`, `targets default`.
5. Discovery results are cached in state with root mtimes; `targets --rescan` forces a rescan. Unknown flavors and version/interface disagreements produce warnings, not failures.
6. Game-running detection: scan `/proc/<pid>/{cmdline,environ}` of own-user processes; a target is running if a process exe basename matches the target's exe (case-insensitive) and its `WINEPREFIX` (or cmdline path) resolves under the target's install root.

### 5.3 Sources and resolution

```rust
trait Source {
    fn id(&self) -> SourceId;
    fn resolve(&self, r: &Ref, t: &Target, ch: Channel) -> Result<Release>;      // concrete file for this client
    fn latest(&self, many: &[&Installed], t: &Target) -> Result<Vec<Release>>;   // batched update check
    fn search(&self, q: &str, t: &Target) -> Result<Vec<Hit>>;                   // optional
}
```

- Ref parsing accepts canonical refs, pasted URLs (GitHub repo/release, WoWInterface `info<id>-…`, CurseForge project, Tukui), `git:` URLs with optional `#tag|branch|sha`, https zip URLs, local paths, installed addon names, and catalog names/aliases. Ambiguity returns `ref_ambiguous` with candidates.
- Built-in catalog (`catalog/catalog.toml`, embedded via `include_str!`; user overrides in `~/.config/omaddons/catalog.d/*.toml`): `{name, aliases[], ref, families[], notes}` for popular keyless addons, so `omaddons install weakauras` works without accounts. Includes verified 3.3.5 backport repos for the `wrath-legacy` family.
- Resolution: (1) source metadata picks candidates (`release.json` flavors/interfaces, Tukui `patch[]`, WoWI `UICompatibility`, CF `gameVersionTypeId`/`latestFilesIndexes`); (2) the downloaded archive is inspected and the client load-rule engine selects which TOC each addon root would load on this target; (3) the selected TOC's Interface must be compatible (equal family; interface ≥ client's family floor; out-of-date allowed with warning). No loadable TOC ⇒ `wrong_flavor`; a candidate failing verification falls back to the next candidate.
- Channels: `stable` (default) | `beta` | `alpha`, settable per addon; GitHub prerelease ⇒ beta; CF releaseType 1/2/3.
- Git source: GitHub repos via `codeload.github.com` archives (no git binary needed); other hosts via the system `git` binary (`clone --depth 1 --branch`), archived from the working tree.

### 5.4 Install engine

1. **Plan**: resolve every requested change; compute folder adds/replaces/removes; check ownership. Output = plan (what `--dry-run` returns).
2. **Download** to `~/.cache/omaddons/blobs/<sha256>` (content-addressed; reinstall, undo-redo and cross-target copies are offline). Verify source hashes where provided (CF sha1, WoWI md5).
3. **Inspect archive**: addon roots = directories containing a TOC matching their own name (any recognized suffix); normalize `Foo-main/` / `Foo-master/` / version-suffixed roots by TOC name; descend through single wrapper directories; ignore loose root files. Reject: absolute paths, drive letters, `..`, symlink entries, device entries, > 20k entries, > 1 GiB uncompressed, compression ratio > 200:1 (limits configurable).
4. **Ownership check**: a folder owned by another managed addon, any `Blizzard_*` folder, or an unmanaged folder ⇒ refuse (`ownership_conflict` / `protected_folder` / `unmanaged_folder`) unless `--force` (never for `Blizzard_*`) or `adopt` first. Enforced by a `FolderName` newtype that cannot represent `/`, `..`, a leading `.`, or a `Blizzard_` prefix in the mutable namespace.
5. **Stage** extraction under `<AddOns parent>/.omaddons/stage/<tx>/` (same filesystem as AddOns, outside the directory the client scans).
6. **Journal** the intended renames to `~/.local/state/omaddons/journal/<tx>.json` (fsync) before touching AddOns.
7. **Swap**: rename existing folders into `<AddOns parent>/.omaddons/snapshots/<tx>/`, then rename staged folders into AddOns. Also copy the affected addons' SavedVariables (account + per-character `<Folder>.lua`) into the snapshot.
8. **Commit**: write target record, append `history.jsonl`, rewrite `status.json`, delete the journal.
- **Recovery**: every invocation first replays/rolls back any leftover journal (roll forward if all staged folders are in place, otherwise roll back), reporting `journal_recovered` as a warning.
- **Undo**: `omaddons undo` reverts the last transaction; `undo <tx>` reverts an older one only if no later transaction touched the same folders (`undo_conflict` otherwise). Restores folders and SavedVariables snapshots (warns if SavedVariables changed since the transaction).
- **Retention**: last 10 transactions or 7 days per target (configurable); pruning is part of commit.
- **Game-running guard**: mutations on a running target fail with `game_running` (exit 4) unless `--while-running`.
- Invariant: at every instant, each AddOns folder is either the complete old version or the complete new version.

### 5.5 State and files

| Path | Content |
|---|---|
| `~/.config/omaddons/config.toml` | extra_roots, target overrides/names, default target, default channel, per-source enable flags, check interval, archive limits, credentials by reference (`env`, file path, or `key_command = "pass show curseforge"`) |
| `~/.config/omaddons/credentials/<source>` | optional key files, mode 0600, written via unique temp + rename |
| `~/.local/state/omaddons/targets/<id>.json` | managed addons per target (schema-versioned) |
| `~/.local/state/omaddons/history.jsonl` | append-only transaction log `{tx, at, target, ops[], result}` |
| `~/.local/state/omaddons/status.json` | summary rewritten after every check or mutation; the widget's doorbell |
| `~/.local/state/omaddons/journal/` | in-flight transaction journals |
| `~/.local/state/omaddons/net.log` | one JSON line per HTTP request: time, method, host, path (credentials and query secrets stripped), status, bytes, duration, purpose |
| `~/.local/state/omaddons/lock` | flock held by every mutating command; readers lock-free over atomically replaced files |
| `~/.cache/omaddons/` | blobs (zips), HTTP validators (ETag/Last-Modified), WoWI file list index. Never CurseForge responses |
| `<AddOns parent>/.omaddons/{stage,snapshots}/` | same-filesystem staging and snapshots |

JSON over SQLite: hundreds of records, human/agent inspectable, diffable, no C dependency; contained swap if ever needed. All writes: unique temp in the same directory + fsync + rename.

### 5.6 Network and privacy

- One HTTP client (`ureq`, rustls) behind an `Http` trait (real + fixture-replay implementations).
- Host allowlist enforced on every request and every redirect hop: `api.github.com`, `github.com`, `codeload.github.com`, `objects.githubusercontent.com`, `release-assets.githubusercontent.com`, `api.mmoui.com`, `cdn.wowinterface.com`, `api.tukui.org`; when enabled: `api.curseforge.com`, `edge.forgecdn.net`, `mediafilez.forgecdn.net`, `addons.wago.io`; plus user-configured git hosts. Violations ⇒ `host_blocked`.
- `net.log` for every request; `omaddons net-log [--since]` renders it. `--offline` (and `OMADDONS_OFFLINE=1`) makes any network attempt fail fast with `offline`.
- No telemetry. User-Agent `omaddons/<version>`. Credentials are never logged, never placed in argv of child processes, never printed.
- Limits of privacy, stated plainly: an update check reveals the checked addons to the queried source; with a GitHub token or CF key it is attributable to that account.
- GitHub token is opt-in: `omaddons auth github --from-gh` (reads `gh auth token` once on explicit request) or `GITHUB_TOKEN`. Unauthenticated mode uses the `releases/latest` redirect fallback when REST quota is low.
- Efficiency: CF one `POST /v1/mods` batch; WoWI comma-batched `filedetails`; Tukui one list call; GitHub per-repo with ETag validators; bounded parallelism (default 6); retries with jittered backoff on 429/5xx/timeouts; per-request timeouts.
- CurseForge compliance: no CF response bodies cached or persisted; the only CF-derived data at rest are mod id, file id and version string inside install records.

### 5.7 Doctor and errors

Finding codes (initial set):

| Code | Severity | Meaning | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| `wrong_flavor` | error | no TOC this client loads | `omaddons install <ref> -t <t>` (re-resolve) or remove |
| `out_of_date` | warn | loaded TOC Interface below client interface | update if available |
| `missing_dependency` | error | required dependency folder absent | install command when resolvable |
| `nested_folder` | error | `AddOns/Foo/Foo/Foo.toc` | auto: flatten |
| `duplicate` | warn | same addon under two folders (`Foo`, `Foo-main`) | remove one |
| `ownership_conflict` | error | folder claimed by two records | reinstall owner |
| `modified` | info | managed files changed since install | reinstall to restore |
| `missing_files` | error | managed folder deleted outside omaddons | reinstall or forget |
| `orphan` | info | library folder no longer referenced | remove |
| `adoptable` | info | unmanaged folder identifiable | `omaddons adopt --apply <folder>` |
| `update_available` | info | newer release exists | `omaddons update <addon>` |
| `lua_errors` | warn | BugGrabber captured errors | per-addon summary; update/report |
| `game_running` | info | client running on target | — |
| `widget_outdated` | info | installed widget version ≠ binary | `omaddons omarchy install` |

- `omaddons errors [-t T] [--since 1d] [--addon A]`: parses both BugGrabber schemas with a SavedVariables literal-table parser (subset of Lua: `Name = <table>` assignments, tables with `[key] = value` and positional entries, strings with Lua escapes and long brackets, numbers, booleans, nil); groups by attributed folder → managed addon; reports count, first/last seen, latest message + trimmed stack, installed version, available update. Raw `locals` are omitted unless `--verbose` (may contain personal data).
- `doctor --fix` applies only `auto_fix: true` findings, each as its own transaction.

### 5.8 CLI contract

Commands:

```
omaddons                              # = status
omaddons status [--cached]
omaddons targets [add <path> [--name N] | rm <id> | default <id>] [--rescan]
omaddons list [-t T] [--unmanaged] [--protected]
omaddons search <query> [-t T] [--source S]
omaddons info <ref|addon> [-t T] [--changelog]
omaddons install <ref|url|path>... [-t T] [--channel C] [--version V] [--force]
omaddons outdated [-t T]
omaddons update [<addon>... | --all] [-t T]
omaddons remove <addon>... [-t T]
omaddons pin <addon> [--version V] | unpin <addon>
omaddons adopt [<folder>...] [--apply] [-t T]
omaddons doctor [-t T] [--fix]
omaddons errors [-t T] [--since D] [--addon A]
omaddons history [-t T] [--limit N]
omaddons undo [<tx>]
omaddons export [-t T] [> addons.toml]   |  omaddons import <file> -t T
omaddons copy --from T1 --to T2 [<addon>...]
omaddons auth <curseforge|github|wago> [set|status|clear|--from-gh]
omaddons config [get <k> | set <k> <v> | path]
omaddons net-log [--since D]
omaddons omarchy [install [--enable] [--section S] | remove | status]
omaddons agent-guide
omaddons schema [<command>]
omaddons completions <shell>
```

Contract:
- `--json` flag or `OMADDONS_JSON=1` → exactly one JSON document on stdout; human/progress text only on stderr.
- Envelope: success `{"ok":true,"v":1,"command":"update","data":{…},"warnings":[{"code","message"}],"next":["omaddons …"]}`; failure `{"ok":false,"v":1,"command":"…","error":{"code":"target_ambiguous","message":"…","hint":"pass -t","details":{"candidates":["retail","forever"]}}}`. `v` is the contract version; breaking changes bump it.
- Exit codes: 0 ok · 1 error · 2 usage · 3 partial success · 4 blocked (`game_running`, `locked`).
- Error codes (initial): `usage, target_not_found, target_ambiguous, ref_invalid, ref_ambiguous, not_found, not_managed, source_disabled, auth_required, auth_rejected, offline, host_blocked, network, http_status, rate_limited, download_failed, hash_mismatch, bad_archive, unsafe_archive, archive_too_large, no_compatible_release, wrong_flavor, distribution_disabled, ownership_conflict, protected_folder, unmanaged_folder, game_running, locked, undo_conflict, state_corrupt, io, internal`.
- Every mutating command supports `--dry-run`, returning the plan in the same `data` schema the real run returns.
- Never prompts without a TTY; nearly nothing prompts at all because mutations are undoable. `--force` only overrides protections (never `Blizzard_*`).
- Idempotent: installing an already-current addon or updating with nothing to update is `ok` with an empty change list.
- Target defaults: read commands and `update`/`outdated`/`doctor`/`errors` default to all targets; `install` defaults to the configured default target, else the single compatible target, else `target_ambiguous` with candidates and exact commands.
- `--progress json` streams NDJSON events on stderr (`{"event":"download","addon":…,"bytes":…,"total":…}`) for long operations.
- Token-frugal JSON by default (ids, names, versions, counts); `--verbose` adds evidence, changelogs, paths.
- Human output: one-line-per-target status, aligned tables, colors only on TTY, `NO_COLOR` honored.
- A top-level panic hook emits `{"ok":false,…"code":"internal"}` when JSON mode is active.

### 5.9 Agent integration

- `skills/omaddons/SKILL.md` in the repository, identical to `omaddons agent-guide` output: purpose, safety model (dry-run, undo, game-running guard, protected folders), envelope and exit codes, error codes with recovery actions, and recipes for canonical intents: update everything; what is broken (`doctor` + `errors`); install X for target Y; add a 3.3.5 addon from a git repo; undo last change; explain pending updates with changelogs.
- `omaddons schema [<command>]` emits JSON Schema of each command's `data` (generated with `schemars` from the output structs), so the contract is introspectable and snapshot-tested.
- `next` hints on every success where a follow-up is natural (e.g. `outdated` → `omaddons update --all -t retail`).
- Canonical-intent budget: each intent completes in ≤ 2 commands with JSON output.

### 5.10 Omarchy widget

- Source in `omarchy/` (`manifest.json`, `Panel.qml`, `Service.qml`, `Model.js`), embedded with `include_str!`. `omaddons omarchy install [--enable] [--section right]` writes `~/.config/omarchy/plugins/a44.omaddons/` via staged directory + rename, stamps the manifest version with the binary version, runs `omarchy-plugin-validate`, `omarchy-shell shell rescanPlugins`, and `omarchy-plugin-enable`. `omarchy remove` disables and deletes it. `status` reports `widget_outdated` when versions differ.
- `Service.qml`: authority = `omaddons status --json --cached` (local only, milliseconds); doorbell = `FileView { watchChanges: true }` on `status.json`, so any CLI or agent mutation refreshes the bar within ~1 s; background check = Timer running `omaddons outdated --json` every `checkIntervalHours` (0–48, default 6; 0 = only on panel open). Actions run via `Process` with argv arrays and `--json --progress json`.
- Bar: gamepad glyph; badge = pending updates; urgent color when error-severity findings or recent Lua errors exist; dimmed with "updates paused" tooltip while a target's client is running; right-click = check now.
- Panel: target switcher (all discovered targets with family + version label); tabs Updates (with changelog excerpt) · Installed · Search · Issues (doctor findings with Fix buttons executing the finding's `fix`); header actions Update all, Undo last, Check now, Open AddOns folder; progress bar from NDJSON events; keyboard navigation consistent with house plugins; all API-derived strings rendered `Text.PlainText`; only `https` URLs to allowlisted web hosts opened.
- Widget settings (`barWidget.schema`): `checkIntervalHours`, `notifyUpdates` (On/Off), `defaultTarget`, `binary` (path, default `omaddons`), `panelWidth`. Product configuration stays in `config.toml`; the widget never duplicates it.

### 5.11 Rust implementation

Layout:

```
Cargo.toml                 # single package: lib + bin "omaddons"
rust-toolchain.toml        # stable channel
src/main.rs                # parse → app::run → output::render → exit code
src/cli.rs                 # clap derive definitions
src/app/                   # one module per command; pure functions returning typed outcomes
src/output/                # envelope, human renderers, progress events
src/model.rs               # Target, Folder, Addon, Ref, Release, Transaction, Finding
src/error.rs               # ErrorCode enum, Error {code, message, hint, details}
src/discover/              # prefixes, bpsv, flavor_info, pe, realmlist, families, running
src/toc.rs                 # parser + load-rule engine
src/sources/               # mod.rs (trait), github.rs, wowi.rs, tukui.rs, git.rs, url.rs, local.rs, curseforge.rs, wago.rs
src/resolve.rs             # candidate selection + verification
src/net.rs                 # Http trait, ureq impl, allowlist, net.log, cache, retry
src/install/               # archive inspection, plan, stage, journal, swap, snapshot, recover, undo
src/state/                 # paths, config, records, history, status, lock, atomic write
src/doctor/                # checks
src/lua.rs                 # SavedVariables parser
src/fingerprint.rs         # CF murmur2 + Wago md5 folder hashes
src/omarchy.rs             # embedded widget installer
omarchy/                   # QML plugin sources
catalog/catalog.toml
skills/omaddons/SKILL.md
tests/                     # e2e (assert_cmd), fixtures/, snapshots/
fuzz/                      # cargo-fuzz targets
```

Crates: `clap` (derive, env, wrap_help) + `clap_complete`; `serde`, `serde_json`, `toml`; `ureq` (rustls; no native-tls); `zip`; `sha2`, `sha1`, `md-5`; `pelite`; `etcetera`; `fs4` (flock); `tempfile`; `jiff`; `thiserror`; `schemars`; tests: `insta`, `assert_cmd`, `predicates`, `proptest`. MurmurHash2 implemented inline (~20 lines, test vectors from WowUp).

Decisions inside the crate: blocking I/O + `std::thread::scope` bounded workers (no async runtime); API structs decoded tolerantly (`#[serde(default)]`, unknown fields ignored, optional fields as `Option`); `unsafe_code = "forbid"`; clippy `unwrap_used`/`expect_used` denied outside tests; commands never print — they return outcomes rendered by `output`.

Quality gates: `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test`, `cargo deny check`, `ubs` on changed files, `insta` snapshots for every `--json` output and error, coverage tracked with `cargo llvm-cov`.

Testing strategy:
- Synthetic WoW trees built in tempdirs: Battle.net root with `.build.info` + `.flavor.info` for every product in §4.1 (including `_forever_` and `_classic_beta_` running 1.60.x), custom 3.3.5 root with `Blizzard_*` folders and realmlist, unknown flavor folder, broken/partial installs.
- Archive fixtures: normal multi-folder, `Foo-main/`, nested wrappers, loose root files, multi-flavor TOC sets, hostile (traversal, absolute, drive letter, symlink, zip bomb, entry-count bomb).
- HTTP fixtures replayed through the `Http` trait (no network in tests); recorded real responses for GitHub `release.json`, WoWI, Tukui, CF, Wago.
- Failure injection (failpoint hook in the install engine) at every step of §5.4, asserting the invariant and journal recovery.
- Concurrency test: parallel mutating invocations serialize via lock without lost records.
- Property tests and fuzz targets: BPSV, TOC parser, Lua SavedVariables parser, archive inspection, ref parser.
- Real-machine smoke checks against §4.7 (ignored by default, enabled by env var).

## 6. Decisions and rationale

| ID | Decision | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| D1 | Rust single binary | No interpreter dependency; ms startup for frequent widget/agent calls; type-level safety invariants; easy bounded concurrency |
| D2 | CLI is the product; widget is a view | Agents and humans share one contract and one implementation; the widget cannot drift into holding logic |
| D3 | No daemon, no MCP in v1 | Nothing needs to run continuously; agents drive CLIs natively; MCP would duplicate schemas; typed command layer keeps a later adapter thin |
| D4 | Keyless-first, CurseForge/Wago opt-in | CF terms make user keys fragile (non-transferable, no caching, non-developer accounts deletable); Wago needs a paid token; the most-used addons ship on GitHub/WoWI/Tukui |
| D5 | Verify TOCs inside the archive | Upstream metadata is wrong in practice (WeakAuras has no mainline entry); the client's own load rules are ground truth; required for 3.3.5 where no metadata exists |
| D6 | Rename-based transactions with journal + snapshots | Atomic per folder, instant on same filesystem, crash-recoverable, enables cheap undo that makes agent autonomy safe |
| D7 | Stage/snapshot under `<AddOns parent>/.omaddons/` | Same filesystem as AddOns guarantees atomic rename; outside the client's scan path |
| D8 | JSON state + flock, not SQLite | Small data, inspectable, no C dependency, atomic replace is sufficient |
| D9 | `ureq` + scoped threads, not `reqwest` + `tokio` | Dozens of concurrent requests, not thousands; simpler code, smaller binary, faster builds |
| D10 | Widget embedded in the binary, installed by `omaddons omarchy install` | Repo root cannot be a plugin (symlink rule); version lock prevents CLI/widget schema skew; non-git plugins are officially supported |
| D11 | Stable channel default; per-addon channel | Reference defaulted to alpha; stability is the expected default |
| D12 | GitHub token opt-in | Privacy: never read the user's `gh` credentials silently; 60 req/h suffices for periodic checks |
| D13 | Host allowlist + `net.log` | Makes the privacy claim verifiable by the user, not asserted |
| D14 | `Blizzard_*` never mutable, even with `--force` | Custom clients ship them inside AddOns; destroying them breaks the client UI |
| D15 | Detection data-driven (version→family table, product table as data) | New flavors (Forever, anniversaries) appear with little notice; unknown folders still become usable targets |

Goal: a correct, fully tested offline core: every WoW client on the machine is discovered and described, every AddOns folder is inventoried and classified, and the CLI contract (envelope, errors, exit codes) exists end to end.

Scope:
- Cargo package (lib + bin), `rust-toolchain.toml`, lint config, `deny.toml`, CI workflow running all quality gates.

- Test harness: synthetic tree builders for all products in §4.1 + custom 3.3.5 + unknown flavor; `insta` snapshots of all JSON; proptest + fuzz targets for BPSV and TOC.
- README.md v1: what omaddons is, what M1 does, the CLI contract, privacy statement.

Checkpoints:
- [ ] `omaddons --json` on the development machine reports `retail` (12.1.x, interface 1201xx, Battle.net root) and a custom 3.3.5a target (interface 30300, label from realmlist 127.0.0.1) with 23 protected folders.
- [ ] Synthetic trees for every product in §4.1, including `_forever_` (1.60.x → family forever, interface 16001) and `_classic_beta_` running 1.60.x, produce correct targets; an unknown `_xyz_` folder yields a usable `unknown` target.
- [ ] TOC load-rule tests cover every suffix in §4.3, the Forever-loads-`_Mainline` case, comma Interface lists, and 3.3.5 single-TOC behavior.
- [ ] Every command's JSON output and every error code path is snapshot-tested; exit codes asserted.
- [ ] No network code compiled into M1 paths; read commands perform zero writes under game directories.
- [ ] fmt, clippy (`-D warnings`), tests, `cargo deny`, `ubs` all clean; fuzz targets run ≥ 10 min each without crashes.

### M2 — Install engine, network layer, keyless sources

Goal: install and remove addons from keyless sources into any target, transactionally, with undo, crash recovery, and an enforced privacy boundary.

Scope:
- `net.rs`: `Http` trait; `ureq` implementation with rustls, timeouts, jittered retry/backoff, bounded parallel executor; host allowlist with per-hop redirect enforcement; `net.log`; ETag/Last-Modified validator cache; `--offline`; fixture-replay implementation for tests.
- Blob cache (content-addressed sha256), hash verification (sha1/md5/sha256 as provided).
- Archive inspection (§5.4 step 3) with hostile-archive limits.
- Transaction engine (§5.4): plan, stage, journal, swap, SavedVariables snapshot, commit, recovery on every start, undo with conflict detection, retention pruning, failpoint hook.
- Ownership model and protections (`ownership_conflict`, `protected_folder`, `unmanaged_folder`, `--force` semantics).
- Ref parser (all forms in §5.3).
- Sources: `local` (zip path), `url` (https zip), `github` (REST releases + `release.json`; asset-name heuristics when absent; prerelease → beta; `releases/latest` redirect fallback), `git` (codeload archives for GitHub; system `git` for other hosts), `tukui`.
- Resolver (§5.3) with TOC verification and candidate fallback; channels.
- Catalog v1: embedded TOML + `catalog.d` overrides; entries for the GitHub `release.json` publishers in §4.5, ElvUI/Tukui, and verified 3.3.5 backports.
- Commands: `install`, `remove`, `undo`, `history`, `net-log`, `info` (metadata without changelog), `auth github` (opt-in token).

Checkpoints:
- [ ] Keyless installs into synthetic and real retail targets: WeakAuras, DBM, BigWigs, Plater, Bartender4, ElvUI; each resolved file verified by TOC load rules (WeakAuras resolves correctly despite missing `mainline` metadata, or fails with `no_compatible_release`, never installs a wrong-flavor build).
- [ ] A 3.3.5 addon installs into the custom target from a git repo and from a GitHub release; `Blizzard_*` folders untouched.
- [ ] Forever synthetic target resolves `forever` flavor assets from `release.json` fixtures.
- [ ] Failure injected at every engine step leaves each folder wholly old or wholly new; next invocation recovers and reports `journal_recovered`.
- [ ] `undo` restores folders and SavedVariables byte-for-byte; `undo_conflict` raised when appropriate.
- [ ] Hostile archive suite rejected with `unsafe_archive`/`archive_too_large`; nothing written outside staging.
- [ ] A request or redirect to a non-allowlisted host fails with `host_blocked`; every request appears in `net.log` without credentials.
- [ ] Concurrent mutating invocations serialize via the lock with no lost records.
- [ ] `--dry-run` output equals the executed plan for install/remove/undo.

### M3 — Updates, search, adoption, addon sets

Goal: keep every target current with minimal requests, find addons across keyless sources, bring pre-existing addons under management, and make addon sets reproducible across targets.

Scope:
- Install records gain folder content hashes; drift detection (`modified`, `missing_files`).
- `outdated` (per-source batched checks, validators, bounded parallelism), `update` (named, `--all`, per target, all targets by default), `pin`/`unpin`, per-addon channel.
- `status.json` summary schema finalized (per target: counts, updates, findings by severity, running, last check); `status --cached`.
- WoWInterface source: file list index cached per `max-age`, batched `filedetails`, md5 verification, changelog.
- `search` across catalog, WoWI index, Tukui, GitHub (repo lookups for owner/repo queries), with per-target compatibility flags and source attribution; ranking by exact/alias match, then downloads/recency.
- `info --changelog` (GitHub release body, WoWI `UIChangeLog`, Tukui `changelog_url`).
- Adoption: identify unmanaged folders via TOC `X-WoWI-ID`, `X-Tukui-ProjectID`, `X-Website` (GitHub), catalog names; confirm exact version by comparing installed file hashes with candidate release archives; `adopt` (report) and `adopt --apply`.
- `export` / `import` (`addons.toml`: target-agnostic refs + optional pins), `copy --from --to` (installs the same refs where compatible, reports skips).
- Doctor additions: `ownership_conflict`, `orphan`, `modified`, `missing_files`, `adoptable`, `update_available`.

Checkpoints:
- [ ] `update --all` across ~30 managed addons completes in < 2 s with warm validators (hyperfine), < 10 s cold; request count per check documented and asserted against fixtures.
- [ ] Unauthenticated GitHub checks stay within 60 req/h at the default check interval; quota exhaustion falls back to the redirect method or returns `rate_limited` with reset time.
- [ ] Adoption identifies fixture installs (correct source and exact version) by content, and never adopts a folder whose files match no candidate.
- [ ] `export` → `import` into an empty target reproduces the same refs and versions (pins honored); `copy retail → forever` installs compatible addons and reports the rest.
- [ ] Drift detection flags modified and deleted managed files.
- [ ] `status --cached` runs in < 5 ms and performs no network I/O.

### M4 — Agent contract, diagnostics, Omarchy widget

Goal: complete the two user surfaces — the agent contract with diagnostics that explain what is broken and why, and the Omarchy widget for humans — on top of the finished core.

Scope:
- `schema` command (`schemars` JSON Schema per command `data`), contract-version policy, `next` hints across all commands, error `hint`/`details` coverage audit, `--progress json` NDJSON events, `--verbose` detail levels.
- `agent-guide` + `skills/omaddons/SKILL.md` (§5.9), kept identical by a test.
- `lua.rs` SavedVariables parser (fuzzed), BugGrabber modern and r152 decoders (chunked messages, string timestamps, embedded locals), folder attribution from stack paths, `errors` command, `lua_errors` doctor finding, `doctor --fix` for auto-fixable findings.
- Omarchy widget (§5.10): `omarchy/` sources in house pattern, embedding, `omarchy install|remove|status`, validation via `omarchy-plugin-validate`, version stamping, `widget_outdated` finding, FileView doorbell, timer checks, bar states, panel tabs and actions, progress, keyboard navigation, optional desktop notifications on new updates.

Checkpoints:
- [ ] Canonical intents (§5.9) each complete in ≤ 2 commands with JSON output; recipes in SKILL.md executed as e2e tests.
- [ ] `schema` output validates every snapshot-tested JSON response.
- [ ] `errors` parses recorded modern and r152 `!BugGrabber.lua` fixtures, attributes errors to the right managed addons, and omits locals by default; Lua parser fuzzed ≥ 30 min without crashes.
- [ ] `doctor --fix` repairs `nested_folder` as an undoable transaction.
- [ ] The embedded plugin passes `omarchy-plugin-validate`; `omaddons omarchy install --enable` produces a working widget on the development machine.
- [ ] A mutation made from a terminal is reflected in the bar within ~1 s without polling; panel open performs no network I/O.
- [ ] Widget shows correct states for: updates pending, error findings, client running, no targets.

### M5 — Optional accounts, release engineering

Goal: add CurseForge and Wago as strictly optional sources that degrade cleanly without credentials, and ship reproducible releases.

Scope:
- Credentials: `auth <source> set|status|clear` (stdin input, 0600 files via unique temp + rename), env vars, `key_command`; validation calls; credentials never logged or passed via argv.
- CurseForge source: search, batched `POST /v1/mods`, files, download with `x-api-key` on CDN, `allowModDistribution=false` → `distribution_disabled` with website URL and `import` flow for browser-downloaded zips (match by expected file name in `~/Downloads`), gameVersionTypeId mapping (§4.5), changelog, fingerprint adoption (MurmurHash2 folder fingerprint, `POST /v1/fingerprints/1`), no CF data cached or persisted beyond ids/version strings.
- Wago source (token): search, `_recents` update checks, `_match` adoption (MD5 folder hash), downloads with token.
- Release engineering: version scheme, changelog, static `x86_64-unknown-linux-musl` build, release artifacts with checksums, installer, shell completions and man page (`clap_mangen`), `cargo audit` in CI, README final.

Checkpoints:
- [ ] With a CF key: search, install, update and fingerprint adoption pass against recorded fixtures and a live smoke test; `distribution_disabled` flow imports a browser-downloaded zip.
- [ ] Without credentials: CF/Wago refs fail with `source_disabled`/`auth_required` and actionable hints; no CF or Wago host ever appears in `net.log`.
- [ ] No CurseForge response data present under `~/.cache/omaddons` or state beyond ids/version strings (asserted by test).
- [ ] Release build is reproducible from a tag; binary < 10 MB; installer verifies checksums.

## 8. Risks and open questions

- CurseForge policy: personal keys may be revoked or terms enforced; mitigated by D4 (never required).
- Forever launch layout (product `wowf` / `_forever_` / interface 16001 / `_Forever` suffix) is pre-launch data; mitigated by D15 and fixtures that cover both beta and launch layouts.
- Keyless coverage of the long tail (e.g. Details! is not on GitHub releases): WoWI, URL/zip import, and optional CF cover the gap.
- 3.3.5 ecosystem has no registry: catalog entries plus git/url sources are the realistic ceiling; TOC verification guards against retail builds landing in the legacy client.
- GitHub unauthenticated quota (60/h): sized for periodic checks; opt-in token and redirect fallback for heavy use.
- Modern `AddOns.txt` format and storage of the out-of-date checkbox are unverified; features depending on them are optional.
- Running-client detection under Wine relies on `/proc` cmdline/environ conventions; false negatives degrade to a warning, never data loss (transactions remain atomic).
- Scope creep (WeakAuras strings, profiles, TUI, MCP) is excluded by the non-goals.

## 9. Confidence assessment

- High: reliability, privacy and agent-ergonomics claims. Each maps to a defect observed in the reference implementation (§3) and is proven by a specific test (failure injection, concurrency, hostile archives, allowlist, contract snapshots).
- Medium: keyless coverage of what users actually run (strong for the most-used addons, weaker for the long tail); Forever's final layout.
- Low: whether CurseForge tolerates personal keys in a local tool. Nothing depends on it.

## 10. Milestone status

- [ ] M1 — Core, discovery, inventory
- [ ] M2 — Install engine, network layer, keyless sources
- [ ] M3 — Updates, search, adoption, addon sets
- [ ] M4 — Agent contract, diagnostics, Omarchy widget
- [ ] M5 — Optional accounts, release engineering

**D16 — No CI. A local gate runs before every commit that changes code.**

This replaces the CI references in the description: M1's scope item "CI workflow running all quality gates" and M5's "`cargo audit` in CI".

- **Repository status.** The repository stays private until the project fully works on the owner's own setup. Open-sourcing happens only once the owner is confident in the project, and CI gets reconsidered then, not before. Until that point there is no `.github/workflows/`, no hosted runner, and no CI configuration file of any kind.
- **What replaces the CI items.** M1 delivers one local command that runs the full gate. M5 runs `cargo audit` locally as part of the release checklist.
- **The rule.** Every commit that contains a code change runs the local gate first, and is committed only when the gate passes. The gate is:
  - `cargo fmt --check`
  - `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`
  - `cargo test`
  - `ubs` on the changed files
  - `cargo deny check`, but only when `Cargo.toml` or `Cargo.lock` changed
- **Not in the per-commit gate.** Fuzz runs, coverage, real-machine smoke tests (gated behind an environment variable) and benchmarks. These run at milestone checkpoints.
- **What counts as a code change:** any staged change to a file that is compiled into the binary or used by the build or the test suite.
  - `*.rs` files under `src/`, `tests/`, `fuzz/` and `benches/`, plus `build.rs`
  - `Cargo.toml`, `Cargo.lock`, `rust-toolchain.toml`, `deny.toml`, and clippy/rustfmt configuration
  - Assets embedded in the binary:
    - `omarchy/**` (the QML, JS and manifest are embedded with `include_str!`)
    - `catalog/**`
    - `skills/omaddons/SKILL.md` (a test asserts it is identical to the `agent-guide` output)
  - Test fixtures and `insta` snapshots: `tests/fixtures/**` and `**/snapshots/**`
- **What does not count as a code change** (the gate may be skipped): `.beads/**`, `README.md`, `CLAUDE.md`/`AGENTS.md`, `.gitignore`, and any other Markdown or documentation that is not embedded in the binary.
- **Mixed commits.** A commit that contains both kinds counts as a code change.
